scope: Connected whole-character support and landing batch: visible soles, pelvis/knees, slope orientation, impact recovery, ground gait continuity, actions, camera and save/UI regressions. Full project goal remains active.
findings: Collider grounding did not guarantee visible sole contact: baseline normal-input snapshots show several centimetres of hovering and occasional penetration during gait blending.
A tilted standing foot can lift its sole beyond a straight leg reach if pelvis height is calculated before the tilt.
Temporal settling initially left the very first support frame about 3.1 cm above the floor for all six body/height profiles.
Ground gait phase was not restored when leaving Airborne.
changes: Compose a bounded player visual-support solver into the existing final SkeletonModifier after moving-leg overlay and before weapon placement.

Select sparse sole samples from the existing skinned boot mesh, including skin binds and active morphs. Match pelvis height, two-bone leg reach and foot tilt to physical surface rays; retain authored swing lift.

Account for tilted soles before pelvis reach; fit new support immediately and avoid lagging downward pelvis reach. Keep collider, jump/move speed, input mappings and world position authoritative and unchanged.

Use the actual existing impact detection to drive a transient 0.24-second landing compression. Preserve foot contact during compression, recover to idle and reset transient state on jump/world-load mode/ground guard/furniture/death.
Restore normalized ground gait phase when leaving Airborne.
Cache morphed sole vertices and skip settled sub-millimetre IK work to reduce isolated modifier cost.

Extend existing mandatory locomotion smoke and graphical normal-input fixture with independent all-vertex skin/morph acceptance; add reproducible slope/stair views. No workflow gate or timeout was relaxed.

verification_notes: Slope and first-frame candidate failures were corrected in runtime while keeping the independent -1.5 cm/+2 cm acceptance bounds.
Static pose fixtures explicitly disable controller physics after node readiness; physical jump and normal-input graphical scenarios remain separate.
A new standalone SceneTree view initially referenced autoload names too early; the driver now accesses them after startup. This was a QA compilation error, not an in-game failure.
Existing source-world exit warning of 79 ObjectDB instances remains; the current change does not declare it resolved.
Logs committed here normalize CRCRLF to LF. Original captured streams remain under build/acceptance.
delivery: Current source project build/stability. No new local PCK/installer or stable publication; latest-commit remote gates pending after push.
remaining: No new human or wardrobe meshes; owner-rejected overall models, shoulder/garment deformation and artistic acceptance remain open.
Height/normal support is not complete X/Z foot-plant locking or turn/start/stop animation; moving-platform, uneven rock/edge and full-terrain acceptance remain open.
Procedural impact compression is not a complete authored takeoff/landing animation set.
The solver currently covers Player rigs using WeaponGrip; it is not claimed integrated into all NPC rigs or animals.
Graphical checks use automated action input and observer cameras, not manual free roam or a new full city journey.
No world FPS, RAM budget, global percentage or full project readiness established.
Nature/buildings/fauna art and full living-world acceptance continue under the existing comprehensive programme.
